questions.stem_latex:
On a dark night, two ships, Saga and Hero, sail parallel to a straight coastline on which there are two lights of equal brightness, 16 kilometres apart.

\exfigure{1015_q11_1}

Suppose the coastline is represented by the $x$ axis where the origin $O$ is chosen to be the midpoint of the light sources. It is known that the (total) brightness from the lights on a ship a point $P(x, b)$ is

$$l = \dfrac{1}{b^2 + (x+8)^2} + \dfrac{1}{b^2 + (x-8)^2}$$

parts.label: a
parts.latex:
Show that $\dfrac{dl}{dx} = -\dfrac{2P}{Q}$, where

$P = \left[(x+8)\left(b^2 + (x-8)^2\right)^2 + (x-8)\left(b^2 + (x+8)^2\right)^2\right]$ AND

$Q = \left[\left(b^2 + (x+8)^2\right)^2 \left(b^2 + (x-8)^2\right)^2\right]$

parts.label: b
parts.latex:
To answer (b) and (c), you may assume the following factorisation:

$$P = 2x\left(x^2 + 64 + b^2 + 16\sqrt{64 + b^2}\right)\left(x^2 + 64 + b^2 - 16\sqrt{64 + b^2}\right)$$

Saga sails parallel to the coast at a distance 15 km from the coast.

By considering $\dfrac{dl}{dx}$, show that, as Saga sails from left to right, the brightness on Saga increases to a maximum when $x = 0$ and then decreases.

parts.label: c
parts.latex:
Hero sails parallel to the coast at a distance 6 km from the coast.

Describe how the brightness on Hero changes as Hero sails from left to right. Give clear reasons for your answer.

solutions.latex:
$f'(x) = -5x^4+45x^2$, $f''(x) = -20x^3+90x$.

For stationary points, $f'(x)=0$: $-5x^2(x^2-9) = 0$, so $-5x^2(x+3)(x-3)=0$, $x = 0, \pm 3$.

$f''(0) = 0$; $f''(-0.1) = -8.98$, $f''(0.1) = 8.98$, so there is a change in concavity: horizontal point of inflection at $x=0$.

$f''(3) = -270$, so local maximum. $f''(-3) = 270$, so local minimum.

$f(0)=0$, $f(3)=162$, $f(-3)=-162$.

Horizontal point of inflection at $(0,0)$; local minimum at $(-3,-162)$; local maximum at $(3,162)$.

For points of inflection, $f''(x)=0$: $-20x^3+90x = 0$, $-10x(2x^2-9)=0$, $x = 0, \pm\dfrac{3}{\sqrt2}$.

$$\begin{array}{c|cccccc} x & -2.5 & -\frac{3}{\sqrt2} & -2 & 2 & \frac{3}{\sqrt2} & 2.5 \\ \hline f''(x) & 87.5 & 0 & -20 & 20 & 0 & -87.5 \end{array}$$

Change in concavity, so points of inflection at $x = \pm\dfrac{3}{\sqrt2}$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: solving f''(x)=0; 1: testing change in concavity and conclusion

solutions.latex: $x = 1$, so 1 m to the right of the origin.

$x = 1 - 2\sin 2t$, $\dot x = -4\cos 2t$.

For $\dot x = 0$: $-4\cos 2t = 0$, $2t = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, $t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

$x = 1 - 2\sin\left(2\times\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = -1$.

After $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ s it is stationary 1 m to the left of the origin.

solutions.latex:
Given $b=15$:

$\dfrac{dl}{dx} = \dfrac{-4x\left(x^2+64+15^2+16\sqrt{64+15^2}\right)\left(x^2+64+15^2-16\sqrt{64+15^2}\right)}{\left(15^2+(x+8)^2\right)^2\left(15^2+(x-8)^2\right)^2}$

For stationary points, $\dfrac{dl}{dx}=0$: $-4x(x^2+561)(x^2+17)=0$, so $x=0$ (only real solution).

The denominator is $>0$ for all $x\in\mathbb R$ and $(x^2+561)(x^2+17)>0$ for all $x\in\mathbb R$, so $\dfrac{dl}{dx}$ changes with the sign of $-4x$.

Therefore for $x<0$, $\dfrac{dl}{dx}>0$; for $x=0$, $\dfrac{dl}{dx}=0$; and for $x>0$, $\dfrac{dl}{dx}<0$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: substituting b=15 into dl/dx; 1: x=0 only stationary point; 1: sign of dl/dx either side of x=0

solutions.latex:
$\dfrac{dl}{dx} = \dfrac{-4x\left(x^2+64+6^2+16\sqrt{64+6^2}\right)\left(x^2+64+6^2-16\sqrt{64+6^2}\right)}{\left(6^2+(x+8)^2\right)^2\left(6^2+(x-8)^2\right)^2}$

For stationary points, $\dfrac{dl}{dx}=0$: $-4x(x^2+260)(x^2-60)=0$, so $x=0,\ \pm\sqrt{60}$.

$$\begin{array}{c|ccccccc} x & -8 & -\sqrt{60} & -1 & 0 & 1 & \sqrt{60} & 8 \\ \hline \dfrac{dl}{dx} & \dfrac{2}{5329} & 0 & -0.0006 & 0 & 0.0006 & 0 & -\dfrac{2}{5329} \end{array}$$

(slopes: up, down, up, down)

The brightness increases to a maximum at $x=-\sqrt{60}$, then decreases to a minimum at $x=0$, then increases to another maximum at $x=\sqrt{60}$, then decreases.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: stationary points x=0, ±√60; 1: sign table of dl/dx; 1: correct description
